title: Compatibility of degree-zero identifications
statement: For a morphism of schemes f:X→Y and y∈Y, there exist an O_(Y,y)-linear equivalence from the ordinary direct-image stalk of O_X to its zeroth derived direct-image stalk, and an isomorphism from the formal-fibre zeroth cohomology system to its section system [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology], such that every canonical theta sends the class of each germ of a section, under those identifications, to section pullback along the formal-fibre inclusion. The formula is the degree-zero dictionary formula; the two identifications are chosen jointly, not arbitrary. In addition, the underlying linear map of the chosen stalk equivalence is exactly the stalk of the canonical degree-zero direct-image augmentation.

proof.text: The direct-image functor preserves finite limits. Its degree-zero augmentation is an isomorphism, and taking the module stalk preserves this isomorphism. The underlying linear map is bijective, so LinearEquiv.ofBijective constructs a with that exact underlying map. Its toLinearMap equals the canonical stalk augmentation by reflexivity; retain this equality in the conclusion.

Apply the augmentation compatibility statement to get b and the pullback equation for the fixed augmentation map. This is precisely the underlying map of the constructed a, so the joint existential follows definitionally. Return a, its canonical-map equality, b and the germ formula.

lean.statement:
theorem formalFunctions_degreeZero_compatibility {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : Y) :
    ∃ a : ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))) ≃ₗ[
          Y.presheaf.stalk y]
        formalFunctionsStalk f y (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0,
      a.toLinearMap = ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y).map
        ((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).toRightDerivedZero.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))).hom ∧
      ∃ b : formalFibreCohomologySystem f y (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0 ≅
          formalFibreSectionsSystem f y,
        ∀ (n : ℕ)
          (θ : formalFunctionsStalk f y (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0 →ₗ[
            Y.presheaf.stalk y]
            formalFibreCohomologyLocal f y (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0 n),
          IsFormalFunctionsTheta f y (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0 n θ →
          ∀ (V : Y.Opens) (hy : y ∈ V)
            (hV : (⊤ : (formalFibre f y n).Opens) ≤
              (formalFibreι f y n) ⁻¹ᵁ (f ⁻¹ᵁ V)) (t : Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ V)),
            (b.hom.app (op n)) (θ (a (TopCat.Presheaf.germ
              ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
                (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).val.presheaf V y hy t))) =
              (formalFibreι f y n).appLE (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) ⊤ hV t

statement_change.old_statement: the compatibility predicate in the target theorem, for given a and b

old_proof.text: Under the stalk and system identifications, evaluate the defining IsFormalFunctionsTheta equation on the degree-zero augmentation class of a germ. The containment hypothesis identifies restriction to the whole fibre with the displayed pullback section, yielding the formula.

statement_change.what: Arbitrary a and b cannot satisfy this formula: for f=id of Spec Q and t=1, replacing the canonical system identification b by -b changes 1 to -1, while IsFormalFunctionsTheta does not mention a or b. Choose the identifications jointly instead, construct a from the degree-zero augmentation, and leave only the canonical augmentation-to-fibre-system compatibility obligation. The chosen a is also required to have the canonical augmentation as its underlying linear map. This stronger conclusion distinguishes compatibility from the already-stated dictionary and exposes the construction rather than duplicating the dictionary theorem.
